authoredFrom: M60 ONTOLOGY PASS 3, 2026-10-03. Both shapes were found by MEASURING production parseFile over the corpus, not by reading the analyzer. Instruments committed beside this file. (1) The phantom-constraint probe is validation/m14/fixtures/sql/pass3-phantom-constraint.mts, and it decides with a PARSE-TREE ORACLE rather than a heuristic, because the heuristic cannot: phpMyAdmin's resources/sql/create_tables.sql line 68 writes UNIQUE KEY `db_name` (`db_name`,`table_name`) — a real index named after one of its own columns — so 'a constant whose name equals a column name' flags a true declaration. Oracle-validated before the fix: 53 phantom declarations in 22 files, after: 0, with the same oracle clearing 4 legitimate same-name indexes on both runs. The exemplars are boundary/internal/db/schema/migrations/oss/postgres/0/07_auth.up.sql, where two constant:scope_id were published under auth_account at lines 90 and 94 — one per foreign key, both named after auth_method's first referenced column — against the real property:scope_id at line 72. (2) The disambiguator measurement is validation/m14/fixtures/sql/pass3-incoming.mts over 1,955 corpus files: a `contains` edge names its member by BARE NAME, and SQL makes bare-name collisions ordinary, so the reverse walk in src/lsp/impact.ts matches on name alone and picks a winner by a rule nobody chose. Before the phantom fix, bare-name resolution was unique for 9,374 of 11,305 contains edges (82.9%) and (name, ownerName) within the file for 11,204 (99.1%), leaving 100 that no per-edge rule could separate. After both fixes: 11,444 of 11,492 (99.59%), with 0 edges lacking the key.
comment: Three sections, and the section order is the argument. Section 1 forbids the phantom: a `constant` named after a column of ANOTHER table, which is a declaration the file does not contain. Section 2 REQUIRES the shapes that a too-eager fix would delete — MySQL's UNIQUE KEY <name> (cols), whose index name IS a direct identifier, and a genuine index named after its own column. Without section 2 the fixture would pass for an analyzer that simply stopped emitting constraint symbols, which is the failure mode of every forbid-only fixture. Section 3 pins metadata.memberKind on both ends of the same-name collision, from BOTH emission sites: the ordinary table-then-index order (createSymbol) and the index-before-table order (the explicit call, which exists because createSymbol emits nothing when the owner is not declared yet). Four of the expectRelationships rows are forbid-side in spirit — they require memberKind to be present AND different, which a payload-only key could not do, because the dedup key would have collapsed the pair to one edge.
